title: context returns a definition twice, and outline doubles every def and lists every call as a ref
body:
`intent search --context forget_snapshot --json` returns the definition row `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs:3917-3922 def forget_snapshot` twice, with one ref (backup.rs:279). `intent search --outline native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/backup.rs` lists every definition twice (remedy :60, default :101, from_project :136, ...) and lists every call site as a `ref` row (to_string, map_err, join, format, clone, ...), so the outline of a 400-line file is a call list with each def doubled. Two consequences for the reader the index exists for: an LLM told to ask the index whether a name already exists (CLAUDE.md, in-plan, in-review: `intent search --kind def <name>`) is answered twice for a name defined once, which reads as a Highlander violation that is not there; and `--outline` does not outline. The duplicate is likely two captures of one symbol (a name node and its enclosing item, or two grammar queries), and the outline should carry defs only unless asked for refs.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): two tags patterns matching one node stored one symbol twice; the symbol reads are `SELECT DISTINCT`, which also cures stores that already hold the duplicates. `--outline` lists what a file defines, and its references only with `--kind ref` (CLI and MCP). Before: `--context forget_snapshot` returned the def twice and the outline doubled every def and listed every call. After: the def once; the outline of backup.rs 14 defs, 0 refs, 0 duplicates; with `--kind ref`, 57 ref rows.
